public_payload.normalized_proposition: Nobody actually knows how much AI is going to cost them in any given quarter, so current token spend is entirely experimental, which is why organizations keep burning through their tokens so fast.

statement.excerpt: The problem is simple: nobody actually knows how much AI is going to cost them in any given quarter. This means that the current token spend you’re seeing is entirely experimental, which is why organizations keep burning through their tokens so fast.

from_speaker: which is why organizations keep burning through their tokens so fast
our_interpretation: The plain reading concerns practical quarterly budget predictability, not perfect advance knowledge of every dollar.
The claim makes a broad assertion that enterprise token spending lacks reliable forecasts and established uses, and that this experimentation causes rapid budget exhaustion.
A few overruns cannot establish the broad assertion, while evidence of reliable forecasts and established production spending would count against it.
The relevant spending practices are those current at the May 19 post; older and later surveys are context unless they describe that period.
criteria.support_condition: Representative enterprise forecast-versus-actual records show widespread inability to predict quarterly token costs, and usage records establish that experimental activity causes rapid exhaustion of budgets.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous records show reliably forecast quarterly costs and substantial established production spending, or identify other causes of the cited overruns that undermine the asserted causal explanation.
